prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: checked baggage from bag-drop/transfer induction through screening, sorting, make-up to handoff at outbound load control; aircraft loading excluded. Elements: Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit: records/stages bags keeping flight; sends Oversize Exception Ticket to Image Resolution Desk (confirms authorized make-up position). Bag Tag Printer: unique tags; Calibration Witness Tag; replacement tags only after authorized detail confirmation. Transfer Bag Feeder: sends Late Transfer Bag Card to Bag Reconciliation Station (reconciles bag to flight; Bag Match Query); meters transfer bags without bypassing checks. Induction Tray Conveyor: priority admission subject to scan/spacing; meters to avoid make-up accumulation. Baggage Control System (Velvet): tag-flight link; transfer validation; screening profile; time-windowed sort plan; alternate route only if screening/timing valid; diverts unresolved bags to Secondary Inspection Chute (restricted; retains until disposition); receives Flight Cutoff Advisory; carrier/flight cutoff profiles; records disposition/release state; keeps bag-flight association while pending. Concourse Zone Controller (Mosslight): Recovery Route Card; induction permissive; assigns bags to active lanes. Flight Data Gateway (Lantern): sends Flight Cutoff Advisory; flight identity/departure timing. North Gate Scanner (Kestrel), South Gate Scanner: verify ID, image, record outcomes; South: Manual Rescan Receipt. Primary Crossbelt Sorter (Juniper): Chute Occupancy Note; routes by destination, cutoff priority, status. Image Resolution Desk: routing withheld until disposition. East/West Make-Up Conveyors: controlled delivery. Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit (Orchard): presents after grouping/screening confirmed; keeps bag order/position; reports capacity; receives Carousel Release Slip from Airline Ramp Coordinator only after position/flight checked. Outbound Load Control Desk: reconciles build vs permitted load before closeout. Actors: Baggage Operations Supervisor (Tern): congestion/overload response, recovery and make-up release authorization (within processing window); priority, may defer bags; coordinates build priority with airline. Explosives Response Team (Pebble): security holds; Custody Seal Log. Security Duty Manager: resolves security release holds. Maintenance Technician: isolation, reports lane restrictions. Airline Ramp Coordinator: confirms staffing/equipment/sequence before accepting build. Requirements: interlocks stop feed on jam/door/downstream loss; scan mismatch blocks routing; threat suspends routing until authorized disposition; unscreened bags held; cutoffs include allowances;

New part:
S156: Image Resolution Desk presents the available bag image and exception details to the operator for review.
S157: The operator compares visible bag features with the recorded tag number and the handling data associated with the bag.
S158: The operator confirms that the image is legible enough to support a decision and does not rely on an uncertain visual match.
S159: Image Resolution Desk uses the rescan receipt to confirm that a second image was captured under the approved procedure.
S160: When the image remains inconclusive, the operator requests a physical inspection through the established inspection process.
S161: The identity check verifies that the physical tag is attached to the inspected bag and that its number agrees with the recorded bag identity.
S162: Baggage Control System checks the recorded bag identity against the current routing data before any disposition is committed.
S163: Flight Data Gateway provides the flight data used to validate the bag's assigned destination and service date.
S164: Bag Reconciliation Station records whether the inspected bag matches the expected flight assignment.
S165: A mismatch places the bag on hold until an authorized operator resolves the discrepancy or escalates it.
S166: Juniper holds the affected bag from automatic sorting while the manual disposition remains unresolved.
S167: Kestrel captures a readable tag image when the bag is presented for a permitted scan.
S168: North Gate Scanner records the tag read and image data needed to support an operator's identity check.
S169: Secondary Inspection Chute provides a controlled location for bags requiring physical examination.
S170: Explosives Response Team conducts any security examination assigned under applicable procedures.
S171: Baggage Operations Supervisor approves the operational disposition when the case exceeds the operator's authority.
S172: After the identity and flight checks pass, Baggage Control System authorizes the bag to rejoin its previously assigned screening and sort path.
S173: Outbound Load Control Desk confirms that the bag remains eligible for inclusion in the planned flight load.
S174: Airline Ramp Coordinator confirms any flight-side constraint that could prevent the reconciled bag from being accepted.
S175: Concourse Zone Controller applies the authorized routing state without bypassing required screening controls.
S176: Maintenance Technician uses the witness tag to verify that the applicable calibration status was witnessed before equipment returns to service.
S177: If a route or flight assignment has changed, the operator obtains approval before the bag is released into the revised process.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
